also: it was nice of you to invite me, but no thank you

terms.comment: Here benignē is a polite refusal.

terms.gloss: kind of you to invite me, but no thank you
terms.grammar: bene vocās, “you invite kindly”; tam grātia est, “I am just as grateful (as if I accepted)”
evidence: Plaut. Men. 2.3.36: bene vocās: tam grātia est (Lewis & Short s.v. tam)
Traupman 104: it was nice of you to invite me, but no, thank you, bene vocās, sed tam grātia est
Traupman 104: no, thanks, tam grātia est; benignē
terms.comment: Lewis & Short explains tam grātia est as “I do not accept, but I thank you as much as if I did”. On its own, benignē declines in the same way.

phrases.latin: Vēscere, sōdēs. — Jam satis est. — At tū, quantum vīs, tolle. — Benignē.
phrases.english: Eat, please. — I’ve had enough. — Take as much as you like. — No, thank you
Go home full, the evening star is coming (said after the meal)
